passage: At the bus stand outside Mahua, Deepak leaned against the tea stall and said loudly, "Vikas only got into the district hostel school because his uncle knows the headmaster." A few boys laughed. Vikas felt the words go in like a splinter. He had studied by lamp light for months, but he had also heard his uncle mention the headmaster once, and a small voice asked, what if it is partly true? He didn't argue. He bought his bus ticket and stared out of the window. That evening he went to his science teacher and asked, "Sir, was my selection fair? Do you think I can keep up?" The teacher told him the entrance marks were his own and gave him two areas to work on. Vikas felt lighter, and got out his notebook.

qa.q: Where did Deepak make his remark about Vikas?
qa.a: At the bus stand outside Mahua, by the tea stall.

qa.q: Why did the remark sting Vikas so much?
qa.a: Because he half-feared it might be partly true after remembering his uncle mention the headmaster, even though he had worked hard for months.

qa.q: What did Vikas do that was wise?
qa.a: He didn't argue, and let his work answer. He asked his science teacher for honest feedback and got specific areas to improve.

qa.q: How might Deepak see Vikas's silence at the bus stand?
qa.a: Possibly as an admission, or as a lack of reaction that takes away the fun of teasing. Deepak may also be jealous, but the passage does not say.

grounding: A rival sneers that the protagonist got in through favour; he lets his work answer and asks a mentor for honest feedback.
